mentl/76c3d7c:
Locked 2026-05-07 by Morgan: "I find it strange that there are
places in mentl code where `|>` is... optional... I can't imagine
working code where there COULD HAVE BEEN |> usage but we just...
didn't."

Wherever data flows sequentially through transforms with each
intermediate value used exactly once, `|>` IS the substrate-honest
form. The let-chain `let x = f(y); g(x)` and the pipe-chain
`y |> f |> g` produce identical graphs — but the pipe form has the
topology ON THE PAGE; the let form hides it behind temporary names.
Per Anchor 6 (Write Mentl like Mentl) + DESIGN.md §2 ("the shape on
the page IS the computation graph"), the let form is foreign-fluency
drift.

  lands without a whole-file pipe-chain audit is deferred-by-omission

- Lists six audit categories: let-chains, recursion-with-`++`, nested

two-top/7688255:
The scrub loop survived yesterday's fix. The debounce keyed on the
exact target frame, which holds in a unit test and dies on a phone: a
held finger jitters a pixel or two every report, and on any real tape
one pixel is several frames, so every report computed a "new" target.
The seek re-fired every frame, each backward jitter restored a snapshot
and re-chased at 64x, and the playhead thrashed exactly as before.

The anchor now stores the finger's window-fraction x and a seek fires
only when the finger moves SCRUB_DEADZONE (1.2% of the width, roughly
4x any sensor jitter, ~80 stops across the strip) past the spot that
last fired. The anchor moves only on fire, so jitter cannot random-walk
it across the threshold. One finger owns the strip (lowest touch id);
two touches alternating positions would defeat any debounce.

The old test asserted the frame-exact behavior that failed; it is now a
jitter test plus a 600-report soak at +/-3 px that the first cut fails.
No sim change; SIM_VERSION untouched.

two-top/76f3de9:
The nightly Fuzz Soak workflow on Phase 11's commit caught two
SyncTest desyncs (seed 29 at frame 53/mismatched 51, seed 61 at
frame 177/mismatched 175). Both fired in `replay_sync --fuzz <seed>`
under the existing `check_distance: 2` rollback verification, but
NOT in the canonical demo or any of the sim/respawn/hits unit tests.

Two root causes, both in `hit_boomerang_player`. Phase 1
investigation (component-by-component checksum bisect) confirmed the
divergence was in PositionF / VelocityF / Boomerang values, not
MatchScore or Dead — pointing at the kill path itself.

ROOT CAUSE 1 — Dead as an add/remove component triggers archetype
transitions:
  * Inserting `Dead` on a player via `commands.entity(p).insert(Dead {..})`
    moved the player to a new archetype. Removing it on revive moved
    the player back. Bevy archetype transitions during a tick that
    bevy_ggrs later resimulates produce subtly non-deterministic
    state — the snapshot/restore machinery preserves component
    values but not archetype-table-row positions across the
    despawn-and-respawn that rollback restoration uses for entities
    not present in the rollback target's snapshot.
  * Bisect proof: a hit_boomerang_player that ONLY inserts Dead
    (despawn / score / hit-stop disabled) was sufficient to trigger
    the seed 29 desync. ONLY despawning (no Dead insert) was clean.
  * Fix: change `Dead` from an add/remove marker to a VALUE
    component that's always present on Player.
    `respawn_at_frame: Option<u32>` (None = alive, Some(N) = dying,
    revive at frame N). `#[require(Rollback, DashState, StunFrames,
    Dead)]` on Player so every spawn includes Dead-with-None.
    `commands.insert(Dead { .. })` becomes `dead.respawn_at_frame
    = Some(..)` via the existing `&mut Dead` we already had access
    to from the players query. `Without<Dead>` filters across
    `start_dash` / `player_movement` / `throw_boomerangs` /
    `hit_boomerang_player` become inline `if dead.is_dying()
